football_evidence.question: Can Marshall hold South Alabama to field goals?
football_evidence.assessment: No material disagreement: EdgeDesk and the line are within 1.8 points.
supporting: When Marshall has the ball (the run game against the run defense): Marshall’s offense averages 6.2 yards per carry, and South Alabama’s defense allows 6.9 yards per carry (FBS average 5.1).

When Marshall has the ball (big plays through the air): Marshall’s offense turns 11.2% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and South Alabama’s defense gives up explosive gains on 14.2% of opponent pass plays (FBS average 10.3%).

When Marshall has the ball (big plays on the ground): Marshall’s offense turns 9.0% of its runs into explosive gains, and South Alabama’s defense gives up explosive gains on 11.3% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.6%).

When Marshall has the ball (early downs): Marshall’s offense succeeds on 50.5% of its first- and second-down plays, and South Alabama’s defense allows success on 52.3% of first- and second-down plays (FBS average 42.7%).
contradicting: When South Alabama has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): South Alabama’s offense has allowed a sack on 3.8% of its dropbacks, and Marshall’s defense sacks the quarterback on 3.1% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.6%).

When South Alabama has the ball (the passing game against the pass defense): South Alabama’s offense averages 9.5 yards per pass attempt, and Marshall’s defense allows 8.1 yards per pass attempt (FBS average 7.4).

When South Alabama has the ball (big plays through the air): South Alabama’s offense turns 13.3% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and Marshall’s defense gives up explosive gains on 12.5% of opponent pass plays (FBS average 10.3%).

When South Alabama has the ball (big plays on the ground): South Alabama’s offense turns 6.2% of its runs into explosive gains, and Marshall’s defense gives up explosive gains on 9.3% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.6%).
quarterbacks: Carlos Del Rio-Wilson has completed 90 of 141 passes (63.8%) for 1,023 yards, 7.3 yards per attempt, 6 touchdowns and 5 interceptions in six games for Marshall, and has been sacked on 7 of 148 dropbacks.
Zion Turner has completed 31 of 50 passes (62.0%) for 356 yards, 7.1 yards per attempt, 2 touchdowns and 2 interceptions in four games for Marshall, and has been sacked on 3 of 53 dropbacks.
Jared Hollins has completed 56 of 92 passes (60.9%) for 909 yards, 9.9 yards per attempt, 8 touchdowns and 2 interceptions in four games for South Alabama, and has been sacked on 4 of 96 dropbacks.

Bishop Davenport has completed 40 of 59 passes (67.8%) for 450 yards, 7.6 yards per attempt, 3 touchdowns and no interceptions in two games for South Alabama, and has been sacked on 2 of 61 dropbacks.
